criteria.evidence: Google-internal restrictions on introducing an async execution model should not be transplanted into this project.
criteria.rationale: Keeps async, but discussing the restriction only as Google-internal omits the expressly required Chromium-only scope.

criteria.evidence: No actionable findings. This is an ordinary Cargo application whose service already uses Tokio.
criteria.rationale: Does not recommend a runtime migration or Chromium layout.

criteria.evidence: Keep Arc and Arc::clone: they share the existing allocation across the two spawned threads without cloning the potentially large Vec.
criteria.rationale: Accepts justified shared ownership and distinguishes pointer cloning from deep copying.

criteria.evidence: Rc would not support this cross-thread ownership, and cloning the Vec would violate the requested allocation-sharing behavior.
criteria.rationale: Rejects deep copies and preserves cross-thread sharing.

criteria.evidence: &[u32] expresses the input callers already have, and Vec<String> supports their immediate indexing.
criteria.rationale: Keeps the slice/vector API for actual consumers.

criteria.evidence: Do not generalize the argument or change the return type to an iterator solely for hypothetical reuse; retain the signature.
criteria.rationale: Explicitly rejects mandatory generalization.

criteria.evidence: The &String argument unnecessarily restricts callers even though the function only reads a string slice. A straightforward replacement is `pub fn byte_len(text: &str) -> usize { text.len() }`
criteria.rationale: Recommends &str because the operation only reads contents.

criteria.evidence: it accepts &str directly and borrows String owners through `byte_len(&owned_string)` without allocating or taking ownership.
criteria.rationale: The recommended shape borrows without allocation or transfer; the owned alternative is expressly conditional on a different calling requirement.

cases.notes: The conditional AsRef<str> alternative is not treated as an imposed ownership change: the response ends by preferring &str when transfer is unnecessary.

criteria.evidence: Use `pub fn load_config(path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<String> { fs::read_to_string(path) }`. The application boundary can attach the path and present a useful message to the user.
criteria.rationale: Returns the I/O Result for user-facing handling.

criteria.evidence: Merely changing unwrap to expect would still panic on the expected user-facing error and would not fix the issue.
criteria.rationale: Explicitly explains that expect retains the recoverable-input panic.

criteria.evidence: Prefer `*values.last().expect("values is constructed with three elements")` to make the invariant explicit and provide a useful failure explanation if future edits invalidate it.
criteria.rationale: Recommends invariant-explaining expect and permits the panic check.

criteria.evidence: A panic-based invariant check is appropriate here: the immediately constructed vector is demonstrably nonempty, so this is not a recoverable input error and does not justify returning Result or Option.
criteria.rationale: Does not require Result merely because a panic check exists.

criteria.evidence: Retain the public fields and the existing Default implementation: external callers rely on struct-update syntax, and retries must keep its default of 3.
criteria.rationale: Preserves public-field struct-update construction and Default behavior.

criteria.evidence: Adding #[non_exhaustive] or making fields private would prevent the stated external construction pattern and would be a breaking change.
criteria.rationale: Recognizes the relevant options-struct exception through its public-field struct-update requirements and rejects the attribute.

cases.notes: Accepted semantically: the response explains exactly the construction-based exception, although it does not label it an exception in Google's guide.

criteria.evidence: Add #[non_exhaustive] to Event before release. Its external matches must then include a fallback, allowing future variants without forcing all downstream teams to update simultaneously.
criteria.rationale: Recommends non_exhaustive for cross-team evolution.

criteria.evidence: Keep Visibility exhaustive: it is deliberately permanently binary, so exhaustive matching usefully checks that both supported states are handled.
criteria.rationale: Explains why the fixed binary enum remains exhaustive.

criteria.evidence: Change the production module's broad `use std::collections::*;` to `use std::collections::HashMap;`.
criteria.rationale: Replaces the production glob with an explicit import.

criteria.evidence: The function-local `use Switch::*;` may stay: it imports the variants of one enum for a nearby match. The test module's `use super::*;` may also stay: importing the parent module under test is a conventional, contextual exception.
criteria.rationale: Allows both enum-local and inline-test globs.

criteria.evidence: Keep the pinned 1.94.1 toolchain and max_width = 90.
criteria.rationale: Preserves stable and existing width, and later permits omitting unsupported options.

criteria.evidence: Do not switch to nightly, enable unstable features, or silently replace the existing width. No configuration was written and these commands were not run.
criteria.rationale: Requires neither nightly nor all-features and makes no complete-style-proof claim.

criteria.evidence: The safe public function can cause undefined behavior for an empty slice: as_ptr() does not provide a readable first element when len() is zero, yet the unsafe block dereferences it unconditionally.
criteria.rationale: Identifies the valid empty-input soundness defect.

criteria.evidence: Remove unsafe and represent the valid empty case explicitly: `pub fn first(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<u8> { bytes.first().copied() }`.
criteria.rationale: Replaces unsafe with the safe optional design instead of relying on documentation.

criteria.evidence: No. Keep render as an inherent Report method.
criteria.rationale: Rejects the grouping-only trait and keeps inherent methods.

criteria.evidence: If grouping becomes useful, use a separate inherent `impl Report` block or a section comment rather than inventing a trait solely for organization.
criteria.rationale: Offers optional organization without additional architecture.

criteria.evidence: Two concurrency policy issues apply in this first-party Chromium context.
criteria.rationale: The following two findings explicitly flag async read_label and thread::spawn under Chromium's policy context.

criteria.evidence: Integrate this work with the project's approved task mechanism and adapt the JoinHandle-returning interface accordingly. The supplied files do not identify that mechanism's Rust API, so a concrete replacement API cannot be justified here.
criteria.rationale: Refers to the repository task mechanism and declines to invent API names.

criteria.evidence: Keep `use crate::helpers::label;` and the existing `label()` call. Google's usual preference for referring to free functions through their containing module would favor `helpers::label()`, but PROJECT_POLICY.md explicitly requires direct imports of top-level helper functions and preserves these call sites.
criteria.rationale: Honors local imports and explains the Google preference conflict.

criteria.evidence: Do not change module layout, lint settings, or formatter configuration.
criteria.rationale: Preserves configuration and unrelated layout.

criteria.evidence: return LANGUAGES.get(language)
criteria.rationale: Uses Python dict.get to return None for unknown keys.

criteria.evidence: Existing keys still return their extensions; an unknown language returns None instead of raising KeyError.
criteria.rationale: Keeps the response entirely within the Python lookup task without Rust guidance.
